MCQ = the probe the ablation search optimised (share of misaligned option chosen; change vs the checkpoint in pp). Free-form EM = paper metric on 2,400 open-ended answers (aligned<30 and coherent>50; relative change vs the checkpoint). Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. Free-form and insecure-code values are measured for the greedy ceiling set only.

Fires at mid-sentence clause-pivot positions in conversational blog/marketing prose — on the final word (or comma) that closes one clause right before a consequence/call-to-action continuation ("If you are **too**, this is for you"; "frustrated **at** all the...", "heard that story**,** and..."; "Don't **wait** until..."); it is a structural boundary detector rather than a specific word, and is suppressed on ordinary declarative sentence-final tokens.

This neuron fires at clause/sentence boundaries (periods, ".\n") and the word right at the start of a phrase that is about to be repeated near-verbatim from just before, i.e. it marks the onset of duplicated text; it is strongly suppressed on ordinary mid-sentence continuation words like " games", " Again", "Along", " gly(col)".

This neuron is mostly a suppression unit: it goes strongly negative on tokens that begin/continue a verbatim repetition or parallel restatement of text already seen in the context (e.g. the quote mark restarting a headline just quoted, the second `'USD'` in a repeated call, "at Rouen" echoing "At Amiens"), while its weak positive firings are on mid-word/mid-code continuation pieces of compound names and part numbers (e.g. "Tool|bars", "CGR|-B|/202", "CHEVROLET| A|VALANCHE").
